findings.claim: `PinnedBase`'s docstring explicitly justifies its existence as protection against the exact bug named in the spec's 'The shape' section: adjacent same-typed positional fields silently transposing while still type-checking (the `check_readiness` scratch/home incident that once deleted the ledger). But `@dataclass(frozen=True)` at line 668 does not pass `kw_only=True`, so `PinnedBase.__init__` still accepts positional arguments, and `url` (line 682) and `base_sha` (line 683) are adjacent same-typed `str` fields. `PinnedBase(mirror, base_sha, url)` — the transposed call — type-checks and constructs cleanly, silently swapping the remote URL and the pinned commit. Every current call site (line 943-945) uses keywords so nothing fails today, but the class delivers none of the structural protection its own docstring claims, unlike `check_readiness`'s actual keyword-only `*` it is compared to.
